description: Every browser source the project ships, in one place. The floor checks, the byte budget and the asset gates all read this: a directory that appears in one tool's private list and not another's is a file that passes the check nobody pointed at it, and that is how a source drops out of a sweep. Adding a shipped asset means adding it here, once.

roots.why: Served by the host status service on every pool machine.
Loaded first by every extension service UI, so a break here breaks all of them at once.
Generated files are shipped browser sources like any other, and a generator that started emitting newer syntax would break the floor exactly as a hand edit would.
Copied verbatim into the shipped runtimes and into the raw Go pages, so a break here reaches every one of them at once. Checked at the source rather than only after it has been copied.

excludeReason: *.test.js runs under node and no page loads one, so the browser floor does not reach it.

cssProducers.why: The per-cycle transcript page. Its stylesheet is a here-string inside the renderer and declares its own light ground, so the colors below it are measured against a white this file states rather than one the browser chose.
The directory listing is built in a PowerShell here-string, so a search for stylesheets never finds it.
Loaded beside the pool-control stylesheet and resolves against its palette, not its own.

The refusal page a caching-proxy guest serves carries its own inline style with literal colors. It is provisioned into a guest that by definition cannot reach a stylesheet, so the palette it resolves against is itself.

The lab landing page. Its document is assembled with a strings.Builder rather than held in one raw-string constant, and its style block uses literal colors only -- so neither a search for a page constant nor a search for var(--) finds it.
The page is a Go string literal that defines and uses its own palette in the same constant.
The page is a Go string literal that defines and uses its own palette in the same constant.

cssProducersNote: Every file that produces CSS a browser will apply, whether it is a stylesheet, an HTML page with an inline block, a Go string literal or a PowerShell here-string. 'palette' names the file whose custom-property values a producer's var() calls resolve against, which is not always itself: a fallback written from the wrong file's values is still a wrong color. A search that globbed *.css would report a clean floor over a third of this surface.
inlineScriptProducersNote: Files that carry browser JavaScript inside something that is not a .js file: an HTML page with a script block, or a Go string literal holding a whole page. A sweep that looked for *.js would report a clean floor over every one of them, which is the same as not checking them at all. The floor check extracts each block and applies the same rules it applies to a file.

provisionedPageProducers.why: A whole HTML document written into a guest by a cloud-init write_files block. Every other producer in this registry is reached by extension -- .html, .go, .ps1, .css -- and a provisioning seed is none of those, so a sweep by extension never opens the file that carries the page.

provisionedPageProducersNote: Pages a host provisions into a guest rather than serves from this tree. They are read by a person at the worst possible moment -- a fetch just failed -- and they are the pages least likely to be looked at again after they are written, because nothing in a normal cycle renders them. The exporter materializes each one from its seed so the accessibility and floor gates measure the document the guest will serve, with the server's own interpolation macros filled in.
pageRootsNote: Directories the accessibility gate serves and walks. Separate from 'roots', which names where the scripts and stylesheets live: a page root holds the documents, and one service can have both. A service added to the tree and not added here is a UI nobody ever renders for contrast, focus order or reflow, and the gate reports a clean run over it.
